RoleCode.description:
Platform-shipped roles (ADR-010 layer 1).

Tenants may later compose custom roles from platform capabilities; they
may never introduce new capabilities, which would be tenant-specific code
by another name (principle 1).
RoleCode.title: RoleCode

eip__api__routers__admin__TenantResponse.description:
What an operator is shown about a tenant.

Note the absence: no password, and no secret *reference* either. The
reference is safe to store (ADR-015), but nothing outside the data plane
needs it, and a value that never reaches a response model cannot leak
through one.
eip__api__routers__admin__TenantResponse.title: TenantResponse

info.description: Every capability is exposed through this versioned API; the web application is one client among potential others (principle 8). No endpoint accepts SQL, a formula, or a field path from a client.
info.summary: Phase 1A — platform skeleton. No business intelligence functionality.
info.title: TriVera Executive Intelligence Platform API

get.description: Report that the process is running. Deliberately checks nothing else.
Verify the dependencies required to serve correct traffic.

post.description:
Grant a membership.

``platform_admin`` is refused by the service: it is not a tenant role, and
permitting it here would let a tenant-scoped principal acquire
cross-tenant capability.
post.summary: Grant a user access to a tenant (platform staff only)

get.description:
Every tenant, incomplete ones first.

This endpoint is what makes "failed tenants are visibly recoverable" a
property rather than a claim. Without it, a half-built tenant is
discoverable only by someone querying the database directly.

schema.title: Response List Tenants V1 Admin Tenants Get

get.summary: List tenants and their provisioning state (platform staff only)

post.description:
Create a tenant and build its analytical plane.

**Operator-driven, not self-serve.** Reaching this route requires the
``platform_admin`` capability and an elevation reason, and every call is
audited into the new tenant's own chain. PO-003 raised provisioning's
priority — TriVera is tenant #1, not a special case — but it did not ask
for public signup, and this is not where one would be added.

Safe to repeat. An interrupted create is resumed; a completed one is
refused with 409 rather than silently rebuilding a live tenant's storage.
post.summary: Register and provision a tenant (platform staff only)

post.description:
Resume a tenant whose provisioning did not finish.

The recovery path for exactly the case Phase 1A had no answer to. Returns
an already-ready tenant unchanged, and 409s if another attempt currently
holds the claim.
post.summary: Retry provisioning for a tenant (platform staff only)

get.description:
Return recent audit events for the caller's tenant.

The audit trail is a product feature, not merely an operational log — a
tenant admin can read their own organization's governance history
(ADR-014 §5). RLS scopes the rows; no ``tenant_id`` filter is needed and
none would help if the session were wrong.

schema.title: Response List Audit Events V1 Audit Events Get

get.summary: List the caller's organization's audit trail

schema.title: Response List Sources V1 Data Sources Get

post.description:
Mint a token for a known user.

Note that the resulting token grants nothing by itself: it merely asserts
an identity. Whether that identity may act in the requested organization is
decided later, by ``resolve_context``, against the membership table.
post.summary: [local/ci only] Mint a development access token

get.description:
Return who the caller is and which organization they are acting in.

This is the endpoint the frontend uses to render tenant context. Note that
it takes no input: the answer is derived entirely from the verified token
and the membership row.
get.summary: The caller's identity and tenant context

schema.title: Response List Memberships V1 Memberships Get

get.summary: List memberships of the caller's organization

get.description:
Fetch a tenant named in the URL.

Deliberately accepts an identifier so that the manipulation path is real
and testable. Any id other than the caller's own tenant yields 404 — the
same response as a tenant that does not exist, so this endpoint cannot be
used to discover which tenants the platform hosts (ADR-010 §4).
get.summary: Fetch a tenant by id (rejects any tenant but the caller's own)
